chunks: He said: When the upper lip is cut and eradicated, its wergild is five hundred dinars. Whatever is cut from it is accounted for based on that. If it splits to the extent that the teeth become visible from it, then it is medicated, heals, and knits together, its wergild is one hundred dinars. That is one-fifth of the wergild of the lip when it is cut and eradicated, and whatever is cut from it is accounted for based on that. If it is torn and shows an ugly scar, its wergild is one hundred and thirty dinars and one-third of a dinar.

And the wergild of the lower lip when it is eradicated is two-thirds of the wergild: six hundred and sixty-six dinars and two-thirds of a dinar. Whatever is cut from it is accounted for based on that. If it splits to the extent that the teeth become visible from it, then it heals and knits together, its wergild is one hundred and thirty dinars and one-third of a dinar. And if it is struck and shows an ugly scar, its wergild is three hundred and thirty-three dinars and one-third of a dinar, and that is half of its wergild.

And in the report of Zarif ibn Nasih, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about that, so he said: It has reached us that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) preferred it (the lower lip), because it holds the food along with the teeth, therefore he preferred it in his judgment.

key_terms.دِيَة: Wergild or blood money compensation for injury or death

ai.seo_question: What is the financial compensation for cutting or injuring the lips according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the precise financial compensation (diyah) for injuries to the upper and lower lips, distinguishing between total eradication, splitting to reveal teeth, and disfiguring scarring. It highlights the jurisprudential reasoning attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), who explains that the lower lip is valued higher because it aids in retaining food against the teeth, a functional distinction rooted in the judgment of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (AS). This detailed classification reflects the Shia tradition of linking physical utility and aesthetic integrity to legal compensation.
